llm.summary: The skill largely implements a coherent stock assistant, but there are mismatches and privacy/exfiltration risks (undeclared AI credentials, automatic sending of local portfolio data to third‑party AI endpoints, and an installation script that installs global Node modules).

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md implement a FastAPI + frontend stock assistant (real‑time quotes, limit‑up analysis, shareholder dynamics, portfolio). That functionality matches the name/description. However the registry metadata claims 'required env vars: none' while the code/AI docs expect AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY, AI_MODEL, etc. This registry omission is an incoherence that matters because the AI provider key controls network data flow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code read and persist local user data (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json) and explicitly build a chat context containing the user's portfolio which is sent to external AI provider APIs. The SKILL.md does not clearly warn that portfolio contents and watchlists will be transmitted to third‑party AI services. The skill also instructs installing Node.js/jsdom for pywencai (web scraping) and to run scripts/install.sh which can modify the host environment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry, but an included scripts/install.sh and backend/start.sh are provided and recommended in SKILL.md. The install script and start.sh perform npm global installs (jsdom) and pip installs; global npm installs are higher‑impact than local installs. No unknown remote download hosts were found in the visible code, but you should inspect scripts/install.sh before running because it runs package managers with global scope.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry declared no required env vars, but AI_CONFIG.md and code expect AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optionally AI_MODEL/AI_BASE_URL). Those credentials are proportionate to an AI chat feature, but they are undeclared in registry metadata (incoherent). More importantly, the skill concatenates portfolio/watchlist info into the chat context and sends it to external AI providers — this transmits sensitive financial data tied to the user. If you set an external provider and key, your local portfolio is likely sent to that provider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide configs. It stores and updates local JSON files (portfolio_data.json, stock_codes.json) which is expected for a portfolio manager. No evidence the skill requests persistent elevated platform privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the advertised stock assistant, but I recommend caution before installing or running it:

- Registry vs code mismatch: the registry claims no environment variables, but the code and docs require AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optionally AI_MODEL). Treat that as a red flag: the skill will attempt network calls to external AI services if you supply a key.

- Sensitive data exposure: the backend builds a chat context that includes your portfolio/watchlist entries (from portfolio_data.json) and sends that context to whichever AI provider you configure. If you set AI_PROVIDER to OpenAI, SiliconFlow, etc., your holdings and notes may be transmitted to third parties. If you do not want that, set AI_PROVIDER=silence or do not configure an API key.

- Inspect install scripts: scripts/install.sh and backend/start.sh will run npm/pip installs (including a global npm install of jsdom). Review these scripts before running, and avoid global npm installs if you prefer local/sandboxed installs.

- Run in a sandbox: because the skill performs network scanning/scraping (sync_all_stocks.py iterates many HK codes) and writes/reads large local JSON files, run it in an isolated environment or container first and review network traffic.

- Backup/remove sensitive data: if you install, consider removing or sanitizing portfolio_data.json before starting the backend to avoid accidental upload during AI chat tests.

- If you plan to use AI features, prefer a provider you trust and understand their data retention/privacy terms. If unsure, keep AI_PROVIDER unset or set to 'silence' to force rule‑based (local) responses.

If you want, I can: (1) show exactly where the code sends portfolio data to remote providers, (2) print the contents of scripts/install.sh for inspection, or (3) suggest safe commands to run the server in a containerized environment.
